consequence: Lead-time reliability has no effect on any buffer. Two suppliers with identical demand dispersion get the identical safety stock whether their lead time is metronomic or swings by nine days, and on this network that is not a hypothetical: 16,198 of 17,829 published supplier-period rows carry a non-zero lead-time standard deviation, mean OTD is 15.08%, and lead times run from 5 to 31 days. The second consequence is a screen: the reference's Safety Stock page decomposes a buffer into demand variability and lead-time variability, and that decomposition cannot be published at all, because one of its two drivers does not exist in the implementation. It was withheld on those grounds rather than filled with a term that would have been the whole buffer relabelled.

rootCause: Contract and implementation diverge, and the same class as FORECAST_HEALTH_GRAIN_MISMATCH: the contract states the semantics and nothing enforces them. Policy v2 declares a two-addend buffer plus the apparatus for sourcing, thresholding and reason-coding lead-time variability; the engine implements the demand addend and no part of the lead-time one.
summary: Policy v2's safetyStock.formula declares a lead-time-variance addend, and its leadTime block declares where that input comes from, how many observations it needs and what reason code stands in when it is zero. The engine implements none of it: lead time reaches the buffer only as a mean that sizes the protection window, so four policy keys and one reason code have no consumer and a supplier's unreliability changes no buffer.
